title: RA-VLA: Retrieval-Augmented VLA for Test-Time Adaptation
claim: Existing in-context adaptation methods retrieve functionally irrelevant context, fail to use it, and slow down sharply as context grows.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid; failure rollouts plus latency bar chart
description: A four-panel figure with rounded gray frames. Panel (a), Context, shows a robot observation image labeled 'Turn on the stove' beside retrieved segments highlighted in yellow and labeled 'Functional irrelevance'. A top-right panel is a conceptual icon diagram. A pink oval labeled 'Adaptation Bottleneck' sits in the middle of three icons: a database with a magnifier (Retrieval), two people handing over a flag (In-context Adaptation) and a stopwatch (Latency). Panel (b), Generated Action (Existing ICIL), shows two rows of three simulated robot frames joined by red arrows and red borders. The rows are captioned 'In-context agnostic behavior' and 'Failure under relevant context', and each ends in a red caption on a pink band, such as 'Context ignorance, memorization bias'. Panel (c), Latency, is a bar chart with red bars for Existing ICIL rising with the number of retrieved contexts and blue bars for RAVLA (Ours) staying nearly flat. A dashed line marks VLA without context. A red arrow points to the tall bar, labeled 'Scalability bottleneck!'. Red marks failure throughout, and the eye lands first on the red-bordered failure frames.
caption: Adaptation bottleneck in existing ICIL frameworks. Existing ICIL methods (a) prioritize superficial visual similarity over functional intent in context retrieval, (b) fail to effectively leverage contextual guidance, and (c) exhibit significant computational overhead for larger contexts. While this overhead is plotted for RICL, other ICIL baselines follow a nearly identical trend.
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models provide a versatile foundation for general robotic manipulation, yet they exhibit significant brittleness when confronted with novel task distributions. While In-Context Imitation Learning (ICIL) offers a training-free alternative, existing frameworks suffer from an adaptation bottleneck that hinders the effective translation of expert context to executable actions. This failure originates from superficial retrieval mechanisms and an inherent behavioral inertia that anchors the policy to its pre-trained priors. To address these limitations, we present RA-VLA, a retrieval-augmented VLA framework that integrates behavior-aligned context retrieval with a grounded execution pipeline. By enforcing faithful adherence to functional cues within a scalable architecture, RA-VLA facilitates seamless task adaptation while preserving inference efficiency. Our empirical evaluations across the LIBERO benchmark and a real-world UR5e environment demonstrate that RA-VLA achieves superior success rates and computational efficiency, establishing a robust framework for training-free robotic adaptation.
